$comment: Neutral shipped <stddef.h> (C89 7.17) — the common typedefs + NULL, as language-NEUTRAL data injected by the semantic phase (see README + limits.json). `size_t`/`ptrdiff_t` are pointer-width = 8 bytes on EVERY current DSS target (all 64-bit; LP64 + LLP64 agree on pointer width) -> u64/i64; an ILP32 target would make them 4-byte (deferred D-FFI-STDINT-PTR-WIDTH-ILP32, shared with stdint). `wchar_t` is PER-FORMAT (c106, D-FFI-STDDEF-WCHAR-PE-WIDTH closed): elf/macho i32 (the POSIX width, UNCHANGED) and pe u16 (the Windows UTF-16 code unit) via typedef variants. The pe axis ALSO rides pe-gated duplicate typedefs in stdio/stdlib/io.json (the MSVC corecrt model: every CRT header defines wchar_t; duplication is the size_t 5-descriptor precedent). `NULL` is the integer null-pointer constant 0 (C 6.3.2.3 — the constant 0 in pointer context is the null pointer); the `constants` surface is integer-typed, so it rides as i64 0 and converts to any pointer like a literal 0. `offsetof` is a function-like macro (no descriptor surface for it yet — deferred D-FFI-OFFSETOF-MACRO). * D-LANG-TYPE-IDENTITY-VOCABULARY: the 64-bit aliases are no longer a bare `u64`/`i64`. C defines each as an ALIAS of a standard NAMED type, and WHICH name is DATA-MODEL-dependent - `uint64_t`/`uintptr_t`/`uintmax_t`/`size_t` ARE `unsigned long` on LP64 and `unsigned long long` on LLP64 (glibc vs mingw/MSVC spell them exactly so); `int64_t`/`intmax_t`/`ptrdiff_t` likewise `long` / `long long`. A bare core mints the ANONYMOUS representative, which since type identity was split off representation is a THIRD type matching NEITHER named entry: `stdc_count_ones((uint64_t)x)` fell out of <stdbit.h>'s 5-way `_Generic`, and `unsigned long long *p = &u64var;` became a bare S_TypeMismatch. Each therefore carries a variant selector plus the hir-text vocabulary tag - the SAME 8-byte core everywhere, a different IDENTITY. ** D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-TYPE-ALIAS-SPELLING-KEYED-ON-DATA-MODEL-ALONE (P48 lane st, 2026-09-01): the selector USED TO BE `when:{dataModel}` ALONE, and the sentence above it is a TWO-WORLD assumption with a THIRD world under it - Darwin is LP64 yet spells `uint64_t` `unsigned long long` while keeping `size_t` `unsigned long`, so the aliases that key held together SPLIT. Every arm now names BOTH axes, `when:{dataModel,format}`; the full per-type per-platform measurement is recorded ONCE in `stdint.json`'s `$comment` and the arms here carry its answers for THIS header's aliases. MEASURED for both of them: `size_t` is `unsigned long` on elf AND macho and `unsigned long long` on pe; `ptrdiff_t` is `long` on elf AND macho and `long long` on pe - so neither VALUE moved, only the KEY that selects it. `dataModel` stays in the conjunction so a future ILP32 target matches 0 arms and fails LOUD (D-FFI-STDINT-PTR-WIDTH-ILP32, still open) instead of silently binding an 8-byte `unsigned long` where the platform's is 4.
